nodes.s: sm_live_ · org tier then user tier

flows.name: Scheduled HTTP check
flows.desc: Control plane probes a monitor in its own region

steps.d: Full re-list of enabled targets for this region, diffed into added / updated (by updated_at) / removed.
Sent over a bounded mpsc(8) so a slow Postgres query can never stall dispatch.
Min-heap pop at interval ± hash(uuid) jitter. Paused monitors stay in the heap and are tombstoned by seq.
in-flight set → semaphore try_acquire (fail-fast) → circuit breaker → per-tenant (org, host, port) bulkhead.
No connection pool: connecting fresh is what makes DNS, TCP and TLS separately timeable.
Resolve → SSRF filter → happy eyeballs (250 ms stagger) → TLS → request over h1/h2 by ALPN.
Status + duration + dns/connect/tls/ttfb ms. Unexpected 429/503 classify as Degraded, not Down.
Flush on size or timeout; retries re-send the identical block so the CH dedup window collapses duplicates.
Minute rollup, 30 day TTL. The source for sparklines and buckets under 30 days.
Hour rollup, 13 month TTL. Day strips and anything older than 30 days.

flows.name: Regional agent probe
flows.desc: A stateless agent pulls config, probes, and posts results back

steps.d: Bearer sm_agent_ token plus If-None-Match. A 401/403 is terminal: the agent clears its cache and stops probing.
Region and agent id come from the token, never from the payload.
Sealed check credentials are decrypted only for the agent that owns the region.
304 when unchanged. Variables are resolved here, and a target whose vars fail to resolve is dropped rather than probed with literal braces.
Same executors as the control plane; the agent runs its own scheduler, pool and batcher.
Stable batch_id reused across internal retries so a lost ack is deduped rather than double-counted.
Batch cap 10k, 300 s future-skew guard; org_id is stamped from the region assignment, and rows for unassigned targets are dropped, not rejected.

flows.name: Detection → incident → page
flows.desc: Failing checks become a confirmed incident and page on-call

steps.d: Keyset-paginates enabled targets cross-tenant and reads per lookback tier. This is a poller, not an event listener.
decide_multi applies the region quorum (Any / Majority / All / Count). insert_open returns Option<Uuid>, so only the race winner pages.
The single push edge in detection. try_send drops with a metric rather than stalling the writer.
Policy steps → targets (user / schedule / channel). Who is on call is computed at page time and never stored.
Deduped per channel; a per-incident sharded mutex stops the sweep and an inbound signal double-paging.
Delivery errors have every URL reduced to scheme://host before persisting. Slack's secret is in the path, Telegram's token in /bot<token>/.
Retry base×2^n capped, vendor retry_after hints honoured, then dead-letter. Acknowledge silences further paging.

flows.name: Public status page render
flows.desc: Anonymous visitor on a tenant subdomain, cache miss

steps.d: Wildcard cert for *.{domain}; the operator host keeps its own cert to cap blast radius.
{slug}.{domain} parses to Subdomain → TenantPublic.
Default-deny: only /, /status, /subscribe, /.well-known/security.txt and four prefixes survive. Login and operator API 404 here.
Host resolves the page; a verified custom domain wins over the slug host for link building.
Single-flight per page. On compute failure a last-good layer serves stale rather than erroring.
Six loads in one try_join! so the snapshot is atomic: maintenance, active + recent incidents, markers, paint windows, day presence.
Outage paint comes from confirmed incident windows only, so a blip that never confirmed leaves the day green.
The hour rollup answers "did we check at all", which is what separates NoData from Operational.

flows.name: Badge / JSON status poll
flows.desc: The machine twin of the status page, shared cache

steps.d: Same anonymous surface as the HTML page; per-IP limits are the edge's job.
/api/public/v1/ is one of the four prefixes the tenant fence lets through.
public, max-age=10, stale-while-revalidate=30. A different policy from the private operator API.
Narrower error envelope: code and message only, no field, details or trace_id.
A JSON hit and an HTML hit inside the same window share one aggregator run.
The badge is a hand-rolled ~600 B SVG whose width is capped so a pathological site name cannot blow up the attribute.
One of the few state-changing routes the web layer owns, because possession of the inbox is the proof.
Response is uniform "check your inbox" whether or not the address already exists, so there is no enumeration oracle.
Links are built off the page origin, so a white-labelled page never leaks the app host.
HMAC-keyed token, independent of the fingerprint salt so rotating that salt cannot void mailed links.
Only confirmed subscribers enter the dispatch fan-out. Unsubscribe is a POST for RFC 8058 one-click.

flows.name: Create a monitor over REST
flows.desc: Terraform or an API client adds a target

steps.d: Per-IP limits live at the edge; per-tenant limits are the app's job.
Bearer requests are CSRF-exempt by design; cookie requests must carry X-Requested-With.
sm_live_ prefix narrows the row, argon2 verifies. Token requests must name the org via X-Uptimepage-Org.
Scope check: full_access, exact scope, or same-resource write implying read.
Compiled URL patterns + hierarchical domain deny-list; the platform's own domains and role mailboxes are blocked walking the parent chain.
Advisory only. It exists so the user sees a clean error, not to guarantee the cap.
Basic auth, headers and secret variables are sealed before they reach the row.
The store takes the limit as a parameter, so there is no check-then-act between handler and INSERT.
(count)+1 <= max_targets inside the statement, under advisory_xact_lock(org_lock_key(org)). This is the real quota guarantee.
No push: the registry picks the new target up on its next full re-list.

flows.name: Check now (interactive)
flows.desc: Operator clicks "check now" on a monitor in a remote region

steps.d: Rate-limited on its own category so an impatient operator cannot drown the fleet.
Per-region queue capped at 256, oldest evicted. Single process by construction: the claim and the waiting request must share a brain.
An agent parked on the 25 s long-poll claims the batch; no live holder means 503 PROBE_UNAVAILABLE.
Returned immediately to the holder rather than waiting out the hold window.
Same executor as a scheduled run, plus a header preview and body snippet for the UI.
Reported back with the check id the brain issued.
Pending map TTL outlives the 30 s request wait so a late result still persists.
check-now results are stored; /targets/test results are returned but never written.

flows.name: Heartbeat (dead-man switch)
flows.desc: A customer cron pings us, and silence becomes a failure

steps.d: Capability token in the path, scrubbed from access logs and exported spans before anything is written.
GCRA limiter at 1/s with burst 10, keyed on the token hash.
Last success, start, and failure per heartbeat monitor; the ping log itself goes to ClickHouse.
Anchors are max-merged into an in-memory runtime on each registry refresh, so the store and the executor cannot diverge.
Evaluated inline: no task spawn, no permit, no circuit breaker, no host throttle. Heartbeats never run on agents.
now minus anchor vs period + grace. A missing anchor is Error, not Down, because never having pinged is not the same as failing.
Same result stream as active checks, so uptime maths is identical.

flows.name: MCP write tool from an LLM
flows.desc: An agent acknowledges an incident through the MCP server

steps.d: 401 with WWW-Authenticate → protected-resource metadata → AS metadata → dynamic registration → PKCE S256 authorize.
Audience-bound sm_live_ token; write scopes are never implicit and are flagged separately on the consent screen.
Org comes from the credential and must have a live membership. Uncredentialed callers get protocol discovery only.
Confirmation is requested out of band of the tool arguments, so an injected instruction inside a monitor name cannot forge consent.
The same limiter as the REST surface; MCP counts as reads.
Everything but an explicit approval fails closed. A human decision records NOT_CONFIRMED; a client that cannot ask or never answers records its own code.
Durable audit with outcome Success | Error | Denied. Reads are not audited.

flows.name: Status page subscriber fan-out
flows.desc: A published incident update reaches subscribers

steps.d: Public narration is a separate track from the internal incident state.
Publishing is explicit, so internal notes never reach the public page.
Both cache layers for that page are dropped so the next read recomputes.
The claim is an INSERT into subscriber_deliveries, so a crash or a second replica cannot double-send.
Confirm and unsubscribe links are built off the page origin, so a white-labelled page never leaks the app host.
HMAC-signed with a timestamp header, same scheme as alert webhooks.
Each send records its own result; RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe is a POST.

flows.name: Domain expiry with sticky last-good
flows.desc: Registry flakiness must not flip a monitor red

steps.d: Hard floor is twelve hours, and the picker defaults to a day. An expiry date moves about once a year, so a tighter interval buys no earlier warning and only spends the rate limits RDAP applies per source address.
Circuit-breaker key is rdap:{tld} so one slow registry cannot correlate failures across every customer.
Cross-tenant singleflight collapses concurrent probes for the same domain. Registry data is public, so coalescing is safe and IANA-friendly.
On success, (expiry_at, registrar, last_success_at) are written to domain_expiry_state.
On timeout, throttle drop or 5xx, the cached verdict is served with a served_stale: annotation instead of flipping the monitor.
Rows older than 7 days measured from last_success_at escalate to Error, which is alert-eligible.

flows.name: OAuth login → session
flows.desc: A user signs in with GitHub or Google

steps.d: Enabled methods gate both the route mounting and the login form.
32 random bytes, only the sha256 stored, 10 minute TTL. Carries redirect_after, invitation and link-code context.
Provider halves are split so the shared phases stay identical across providers.
State is consumed with an atomic DELETE … RETURNING, so replay is impossible and unknown state is indistinguishable from expired.
Response capped at 256 KiB. verified_email stays None unless the provider attested it, which is the account-takeover guard.
One transaction: find-or-create user, link identity, create the signup org with an owner membership, and un-delete a soft-deleted account.
Opaque token, only its sha256 stored; 30 day idle and 90 day absolute expiry, last-used writes debounced.

flows.name: Account deletion → cross-store erasure
flows.desc: The 30-day claim has to hold in both databases

steps.d: Blocked with OWNS_SHARED_ORGS if the user solely owns an org with other members.
Tombstones plus a hashed recovery row, all inside one locked transaction.
Sent after commit, never inside the transaction.
Runs under a job advisory lock so only one replica executes; owner rows are locked in id order to stay deadlock-free.
Deleting in PG then CH would orphan rows if the worker died between them, invisible to queries and resident on disk forever.
Runs with mutations_sync=2 so it returns only once applied. Replay-safe by construction.
The queue row clears only after count() proves zero rows across the raw table and both rollups.

flows.name: Browser flow check
flows.desc: A scripted login journey run in a real engine

steps.d: Minimum interval 300 s; the whole kind is gated by plans.max_flow_checks.
The engine bounds its own concurrency; the clock starts only once a permit is held.
{{vars}} were substituted at config-serve time, single-pass. Secrets are allowed in step values but never in URLs or assertions.
Fresh process on a free port with private-network and CIDR blocking, heap and response caps. Fresh process means a fresh cookie jar.
Goto / Click / Fill / WaitFor / AssertText / AssertUrl, executed as JS because CDP key-typing does not populate input.value here.
Passed → Up. Failed → Down carrying "step i/n op: reason". Engine trouble → Error, so a broken runner never reads as a customer outage.

flows.name: Marketing / docs request
flows.desc: The apex host serves bytes with no database at all

steps.d: Same process, same port. Only the Host header differs.
Apex and www classify as Marketing; an unknown host lands here too and gets a branded 404.
Hard-isolated: it may not import storage, domain or tenancy, and tests assert every route returns 2xx with no database.
Rendered once at startup into Bytes with an ETag. Accept: text/markdown serves the authored source, not an HTML round-trip.

flows.name: Telemetry + dead-man
flows.desc: What leaves the process so an outage is visible

steps.d: uptimepage_checks_total, check_duration_ms and the phase histograms, with explicit buckets because agents emit across regions where quantile-of-quantiles is wrong.
Every dropped result is labelled queue_full, target_in_flight, pool_saturated, buffer_overflow or retries_exhausted.
Route label is the matched path so cardinality stays bounded; one INFO access line carries the trace id for the log-to-trace pivot.
A 30 s sweep recomputes agents_enabled_down every pass, so a frozen per-agent series cannot hide a dead region.
Monitors whose covering regions all went dark notify once per episode. Above a quarter of the fleet it is treated as one infra outage and per-customer notices are suppressed.
